edit.description: friction's name-lookup readFileSync catch (~1230-1237) and bare-list readdirSync catch (~1249-1256) swallow every error as absence — split ENOENT (legitimate) from other errors, matching check's own pendingPath read (~1130-1138); surface non-ENOENT as an I/O failure (EX_IOERR).
friction <name> and bare friction against a note/dir whose read fails non-ENOENT (e.g. EACCES) each report an I/O failure, never 'no such note' / an empty list.

summary: flume friction's name-lookup and bare-list catches swallow every read/readdir error as absence, misreporting I/O failures as 'no such note' or an empty list.
tests: friction <name> against a note whose read fails with a non-ENOENT error reports an I/O failure, not 'no such note'
friction (bare list) against a friction dir whose readdir fails with a non-ENOENT error reports an I/O failure, not an empty list
acceptance: Both friction read paths distinguish ENOENT from other errors, matching check's existing split — a non-ENOENT failure surfaces as an I/O error, never as absence.
notes: Sweep finding (posture pass over src/cli.ts). Same bug shape at two call sites in the same command; check's own read at ~1130 already does the split. EX_IOERR is the existing exit code for this class (sysexits.h, per platform-facts.md).
